method: An independent fresh reviewer received the 16 conversations in shuffled order with actual model/effort, version and source metadata removed. It saw the original requests, scripted answers, user-facing final-channel responses and the material criteria. It was instructed to read only that review file. The primary agent independently reviewed the outputs and agrees with the material assessment.
verdict: All 16 conversations materially pass against their supplied requests and answers. This includes 12 new lower-effort conversations and four existing Ultra comparators, not 16 new tests.
rationale: Newsletter prompts preserve spelling/punctuation-only scope. Search prompts clarify symptoms without demanding known causes and preserve evidence/source limits. Radio prompts preserve one-page scope, source and no-new-system boundaries and confirm the end state before rendering. Feedback prompts ask draft-versus-send directly and preserve the final prohibition on contact. Readiness remains conditional on supplying later inputs.

minor_concerns.finding: Several conversations include repeated skill quotations that add procedural clutter.
Presenter-experience answer options A and B overlap.
The unused send option could state final-message approval more clearly. Draft-only was selected and preserved; no permission expansion occurred.
Effort recommendations are judgement about the later task, not measured task-execution performance.

primary_decision: No runtime change from this small batch. Retain the minor findings for broader testing; avoid adding rules merely to polish these familiar cases.
